title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous pages): S is a base scheme and M is a rank-2 vector bundle on S. G = GL(M) and PG = PGL(M), with p: G -> PG the canonical morphism. Grothendieck is studying the scheme of regular unipotent sections of G and of PG.

On the previous page he asked when λε is still unipotent, for ε regular unipotent and λ a scalar. Taking determinants and traces gives λ^2 = 1 and 2λ = 2. Writing λ = 1+ν, these become 2ν = 0 and ν^2 = 0. They cut out a closed subgroup scheme μ'_2 of μ_2 (the page's "H'_2" / "M'_2"). Its ring is Z[T]/(T^2-1, 2T-2) = Z[S]/(S^2, 2S), i.e. Spec(Z ⊕ Z/2) with Z/2 an ideal of square zero. This group is trivial over Z[1/2] and equals μ_{2,F_2} = Spec F_2[ν]/(ν^2) in characteristic 2.

On this page:
(i) μ'_{2,S} acts freely by translation (λ, ε) ↦ λε on Unip.reg(G). Freeness holds because νε = 0 with ε invertible forces ν = 0.
(ii) (47): the quotient is identified with the regular unipotents of PG, Unip.reg(G)/μ'_{2,S} ≅ Unip.reg(PG).
(iii) This looks paradoxical against the chain (48):
- Borels(G) ≅ Borels(PG) via B ↦ B/G_m.
- Each side is ≅ to its scheme of 'unipotent one-parameter subgroups' via B ↦ B_u.
- On those, L ↦ p(L) is an isomorphism.
One would naively expect regular unipotents to be governed by the one-parameter subgroups (each regular unipotent ε = 1+N giving t ↦ 1+tN). That would make Unip.reg(G) → Unip.reg(PG) injective, yet (47) has nontrivial fibres μ'_2 in residue characteristic 2 or over non-reduced bases.
(iv) First guess: the vertical maps (surjective by definition) fail to be injective when 2 is not invertible. He then recalls (49): B = Norm(B_u) and B~ = Norm(B~_u). He also recalls that unipotent one-parameter subgroups of G correspond 1-1 to sections of P = P(M), i.e. line subbundles D, and wants to check this in linear-algebra terms.

The next page resolves the paradox differently. A regular unipotent section of PG does not canonically determine a one-parameter subgroup. ε and λε give one-parameter subgroups G_a → G → PG that agree at t = 1 but have different derivatives at 0 (N' = (1+ν)N + ν). So the map from unipotents to one-parameter subgroups is not well defined on PG in characteristic 2.

Purpose: a careful scheme-theoretic (SGA3-style) description of regular unipotents and Borels for GL_2/PGL_2 over arbitrary bases, presumably as input to the 'équation des lacets' / Galois–Teichmüller setting (PGL_2 acting on P^1).
errors: The previous page asserts μ'_2 = Spec Z[S]/(S^2, 2S) is 'fini sur Z, plat sur Z'. It is finite but NOT flat over Z: the ring Z ⊕ (Z/2)S has 2-torsion. The group is trivial over Z[1/2] and is μ_2 over F_2, so its fibre degree jumps.

Because μ'_2 is not flat, forming the quotient Unip.reg(G)/μ'_{2,S} in (47) needs care. Quotients by non-flat group schemes are not standard fppf quotients; (47) should be read as a statement about fibres of the map to Unip.reg(PG) rather than as a torsor quotient.

The first proposed explanation (non-injectivity of B ↦ B_u off the hypothesis '2 invertible') is abandoned on the next page in favour of the correct one: unipotent sections of PG do not determine one-parameter subgroups. Indeed B ↦ B_u is an isomorphism over any base.

ideas.what: Scalars preserving unipotence of a regular unipotent in GL_2: λ^2 = 1, 2λ = 2, giving the non-flat group scheme Spec Z[S]/(S^2, 2S).
ideas.modern_name: Fibres of the unipotent scheme under the central isogeny GL_2 → PGL_2 in bad characteristic

ideas.what: Free action of μ'_2 on Unip.reg(GL_2) with quotient Unip.reg(PGL_2).
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of unipotent varieties/schemes for isogenous reductive groups (characteristic 2 subtleties)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard theory of unipotent varieties (Springer, Steinberg; Lusztig in bad characteristic)

ideas.what: Borels(G) ≅ Borels(PG) ≅ unipotent one-parameter subgroups, with B = Norm(B_u).
ideas.modern_name: Scheme of Borel subgroups; Borel subgroups are self-normalizing and equal to the normalizer of their unipotent radical

ideas.what: A regular unipotent of PGL_2 in characteristic 2 / over non-reduced bases does not determine a one-parameter subgroup t ↦ 1+tN, since lifts ε and λε give distinct maps G_a → PG agreeing at t = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of a canonical 'logarithm'/Springer-type map for unipotents in bad characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: known phenomena in bad characteristic (Springer isomorphisms, Seitz, McNinch)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine scheme-theoretic check of characteristic-2 subtleties for GL_2 versus PGL_2 regular unipotents. The phenomena are well known in principle, and the page contains a small error (claimed flatness).
